checks.title: Startup via SDK like Sage; init system message
checks.observed: Sage-shaped query() (pathToClaudeCodeExecutable=~/.local/bin/claude, cleanEnv() scrubbing ^(ANTHROPIC_|CLAUDE_CODE_|CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_|CLAUDECODE$), streaming Channel input, settingSources user/project/local, thinking adaptive/summarized, canUseTool) started CLI 2.1.295 on the user's Max login (apiKeySource none, account.subscriptionType "Claude Max"). system/init: claude_code_version 2.1.295, 28 tools (incl. Workflow, EnterPlanMode/ExitPlanMode, Monitor, TaskStop, CronCreate, ToolSearch), 69 slash_commands, terminal_slash_commands [doctor,color,focus,reload-plugins], 33 skills, 3 builtin plugins, permissionMode default, output_style default, capabilities [interrupt_receipt_v1, interrupt_cancel_queued_v1, interrupt_send_now_v1, msg_lifecycle_v1, ...], fast_mode_disabled_reason "sdk_opt_in_required". init arrives at the start of every turn (not before the first message). mcp_servers in the first init was [] while 10 claude.ai connectors were still connecting; later inits list them.
checks.designImpact: Confirms the agent-sdk channel and Negotiated.cliVersion from init.claude_code_version. fast_mode_disabled_reason is "sdk_opt_in_required" unless settings.fastMode is passed (Sage probe() already does this). mcp_servers in the first init can be empty because MCP startup is async, so read MCP state from mcpServerStatus() or later inits.

checks.title: systemPrompt preset vs Sage default (no preset)
checks.observed: Without systemPrompt the SDK sends systemPrompt "" (sdk.mjs: s===void 0 -> p=""; initialize sends [""]). The transcript prompt_snapshot.systemPrompt[0] is "". getContextUsage "System prompt" = 141 tokens without preset vs 3315 with {type:"preset",preset:"claude_code",append}. The preset is accepted and append is applied (reply ended with the ZEBRA marker). Both runs still knew they were "Claude Code" and knew the cwd, because the CLI adds a minimal identity and environment context outside the system prompt.
checks.designImpact: Design issue #7 is real: Sage sessions lose about 3.2k tokens of Claude Code default instructions. Keep the design branch: always pass {type:"preset",preset:"claude_code",append}. Also pass snapshot:true (recommended in the d.ts) so a changed append does not invalidate the cached prefix mid-session.

checks.title: supportedCommands() / init.slash_commands and terminal-only flag
checks.observed: supportedCommands() equals initializationResult().commands (69 entries; fields name, description, argumentHint, aliases, builtin only; no local-jsx/terminalOriented/type flag). Present: goal, code-review (aliases ["review"]; argumentHint "[low|medium|high|xhigh|max|ultra] [--fix] [--comment] ..."), init, compact, context, usage (aliases cost, stats), security-review, ultrareview, loop, schedule, effort (incl. "ultracode [on|off]"), output-style, mcp, rename, clear (aliases reset,new), model, fast ("rewind" is not a command). Absent and answered locally with "/X isn't available in this environment.": skills, tasks, status, memory, feedback, plan, permissions, resume (no "workflows" either). The only terminal flag is init.terminal_slash_commands = [doctor, color, focus, reload-plugins].
checks.designImpact: "skills" is not a command, so the registry must source skills from init.skills / supportedCommands (skills appear there as commands). The "local-jsx / terminalOriented" filter the design mentions does not exist on the SDK surface; commands that only have interactive UIs are simply not advertised, so filtering terminal_slash_commands plus Sage UI commands is enough. "/review" is only an alias, so the menu should read aliases[]. Unadvertised names (/tasks, /status, /memory, /skills, /plan, /permissions, /feedback, /resume) must be intercepted by Sage (as the design says), or they return the "isn't available" text.

checks.title: '/goal <condition>' passthrough, show, clear, interrupt
checks.model: claude-haiku-5-5 (goal evaluator is the CLI's own small model)
checks.observed: Plain-string "/goal <cond>" (and a one-block content array) is recognized in streaming mode: a synthetic assistant message "Goal set: <cond>" (model "<synthetic>", local_command_source), then the CLI keeps working INSIDE ONE TURN. Each unmet check arrives as a synthetic user message (isSynthetic:true) "Stop hook feedback:\n[<cond>]: <reason>". With a one-file-per-reply rule it ran a, b, c in one result (num_turns 6) and d to g (num_turns 8), and stopped when met. NO active_goal message was ever emitted to the SDK stream: the CLI forwards active_goal to stdout only when CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE is set (strings: if(a.CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE){...enqueue({type:"active_goal",...})}). goal_status attachments ({met, condition, reason, sentinel}) are written only to the transcript jsonl. No "met" event appears in the stream; the turn just ends. "/goal" prints "Goal active: <cond> (not yet evaluated)" or "No goal set. Usage: `/goal <condition>`"; "/goal clear" prints "Goal cleared: <cond>" or "No goal set" (all are local, num_turns 0, no tokens). interrupt() leaves the goal active ("not yet evaluated"). A "/goal clear" queued while the loop is running is NOT applied between iterations. It ran only after the loop finished all 6 files (C4c). Usage text is "[<condition> | clear]": no pause, resume or budget subcommands. The CLI can pause a goal itself ("Goal paused · usage limit reached…", strings only, not observed).
checks.designImpact: Passthrough works, so keep the binding. But the claim "翻译器读 active_goal 渲染目标条" is false for a local CLI 2.1.295. Build GoalSnapshot from (a) the synthetic "Goal set:/Goal cleared:/Goal active:" texts, (b) the "Stop hook feedback:\n[cond]: reason" synthetic user messages (iterations = count, lastReason), and (c) the transcript goal_status attachments (met/failed), which Sage already watches. Do not set CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE (broad side effects). Keep controls to clear only. Budget enforcement must be interrupt() then "/goal clear". Sending "/goal clear" alone does not stop a running loop. After Stop, the goal stays active, which matches the design text "目标仍在，下一条消息会继续".

checks.title: origin {kind:"human"} and the ultracode keyword
checks.observed: SDKUserMessage.origin = {kind:"human"} is accepted and persisted on the transcript user record. The "ultracode" keyword produced a workflow_keyword_request attachment (and auto-loaded the workflow-authoring skill) ONLY with origin human. Without origin, no attachment was produced. CLI gate: isHumanTypedPrompt = isRegularUserPrompt && origin?.kind==="human"; the trigger also needs workflows enabled and settings.workflowKeywordTriggerEnabled (default true). No stream/system/status message signals the trigger. The effort level was unchanged. An unknown "/sage-codex-skill-xyz args" was NOT a hard "Unknown command" error in either case: both got an unknown_command_fallback attachment and the text went to the model (1 turn).
checks.designImpact: Design issue #6 is real: without origin human, Sage loses the ultracode keyword (and any other isHuman gate). Keep the branch "用户键入的消息带 origin human，Sage 合成的不带". The ordering concern in commandLayer.rules[3] (that origin turns unknown commands into a hard "Unknown command") is not reproduced on 2.1.295. Unknown commands fall back to the model either way. Removing the Codex-skill rewrite is still right, but it is not forced by origin.

checks.title: Query.applyFlagSettings / settings.ultracode
checks.observed: applyFlagSettings exists and resolves. Session state was read with q.getSettings(), a runtime method that is in sdk.mjs but NOT declared on Query in sdk.d.ts. Its applied field has {ultracode, ultracodeRequested, ultracodeAvailable}. applyFlagSettings({ultracode:true}) flips applied.ultracode false->true on haiku and sonnet (ultracodeAvailable true for both). query({settings:{ultracode:true}}) also starts with it on. On the next human turn the transcript got an ultra_effort_enter attachment ("Ultracode is on…"). applyFlagSettings({effortLevel:"low"}) WITHOUT an ultracode key turned ultracode off (applied.ultracode false although the flag layer still held ultracode:true). {ultracode:null} clears it. No stream event announces the change. ModelInfo has no supportsUltracode field.
checks.designImpact: Confirms the "ultracode=true via applyFlagSettings, re-send it with every effort change" branch. Sage's current applyFlagSettings({effortLevel, fastMode}) silently turns ultracode off, so the adapter must always include ultracode. To show availability, use getSettings().applied.ultracodeAvailable (undeclared in d.ts, so mark it as a version-gated negotiation) instead of a ModelInfo flag.

checks.title: Plan mode round trip
checks.observed: setPermissionMode("plan") mid-session emitted system/status {status:null, permissionMode:"plan"}. The next init had permissionMode "plan". The model wrote its plan to ~/.claude/plans/<slug>.md (CLI behavior, outside cwd), loaded ExitPlanMode through ToolSearch (it is a deferred tool), and called it. canUseTool got ExitPlanMode with input {plan, planFilePath}. Allowing with updatedPermissions [{type:"setMode",mode:"acceptEdits",destination:"session"}] emitted system/status permissionMode "acceptEdits". The model then executed, and the next init reported acceptEdits. setPermissionMode("default") emitted status permissionMode "default".
checks.designImpact: Confirms "批准时返回 updatedPermissions setMode 回到进入前的档位" and "读 system/status 的 permissionMode". Note: plan mode writes plan files to ~/.claude/plans, and planFilePath is available in the ExitPlanMode input for rendering the plan card once.

checks.title: Background tasks, stopTask, perTaskStopAffordance
checks.observed: Background Bash (run_in_background) emitted background_tasks_changed {tasks:[{task_id,task_type:"local_bash",description}]} and task_started. q.stopTask(id) stopped only that task (task_updated, then task_notification status "stopped", then background_tasks_changed without it; ps confirmed only that sleep died). Background shells survived interrupt() with and without perTaskStopAffordance. A background subagent (local_agent) survived interrupt() WITH perTaskStopAffordance:true, but WITHOUT it the interrupt stopped it (task_notification status "stopped", background_tasks_changed []). Closing the query killed all remaining tasks.
checks.designImpact: Confirms #17 and the branch "perTaskStopAffordance:true + task panel + q.stopTask in the same release". Today Sage (no affordance) kills background agents on every Stop. Use background_tasks_changed as the level signal for the task table (per d.ts) and task_* events for edges. close() kills everything, so the reaper must skip sessions with tasks (as designed).

checks.title: In-process SDK MCP image tool (computer-use channel)
checks.observed: createSdkMcpServer({name:"sage", tools:[tool("sage_screenshot", ..., {}, handler)]}) in options.mcpServers. init lists mcp_servers sage connected (source sdk) and tool mcp__sage__sage_screenshot. The handler returned {type:"image", data:<png b64>, mimeType:"image/png"}, and the model read the random word correctly (BOLOMI) in both default mode and dontAsk+allowedTools["mcp__sage__sage_screenshot"]. The tool was DEFERRED: the model had to call ToolSearch first. In default mode canUseTool WAS invoked for mcp__sage__sage_screenshot. In dontAsk+allowedTools it was not, and the SDK warned that canUseTool was shadowed. Handler extra.sessionId is null; extra._meta has "claudecode/toolUseId" and requestId only.
checks.designImpact: Confirms the sdkMcp injection channel and the read-only allowedTools branch. Changes: (1) build one createSdkMcpServer instance per startSession and attribute calls by closure plus _meta["claudecode/toolUseId"], because extra.sessionId is null. (2) Set alwaysLoad:true (server or tool) so Sage tools are not hidden behind ToolSearch. (3) requestPermission must auto-allow mcp__sage__* in default/auto modes, as designed, because canUseTool does fire for them.

checks.title: persistSession:false
checks.observed: Session 228209a3… with persistSession:false wrote no jsonl (not during the session or after close), was absent from listSessions({dir:cwd}) and from the 50 most recent sessions, and getSessionInfo returned undefined.
checks.designImpact: Confirms temporary = persistSession:false (ephemeral:"native"). As the design notes, such a session cannot be resumed after its process ends, so account switches must not close-and-resume it.

checks.title: Block order: slash command last vs not last
checks.observed: [handoff text, image, "/goal …"] (command last): recognized ("Goal set:", goal_status sentinel then met). The transcript stored the handoff and image blocks before the <command-name>/goal</command-name> block. ["/goal …", image, handoff] and [handoff, "/goal …", image]: NOT recognized. The whole message went to the model as plain text and no goal was set.
checks.designImpact: Confirms the adapter rule "交接、图片、用户文字（以 / 开头的文字放最后一块）" (#19). A slash command is recognized only when it is the last content block.

checks.title: '/compact' passthrough
checks.observed: "/compact" emitted system/status "compacting", then status {compact_result:"success"}, then compact_boundary {compact_metadata:{trigger:"manual", pre_tokens:19311, post_tokens:2603, duration_ms…}}, a summary user message, a replayed "<local-command-stdout>Compacted </local-command-stdout>", and a result (num_turns 0). "/compact keep only the code word" was parsed as a command (status compacting, compact_result "failed", compact_error "Not enough messages to compact."). Recall after compaction worked.
checks.designImpact: Confirms the passthrough binding for compact, including "/compact <args>". Render compact_boundary (trigger manual) and the status compact_result/compact_error.

checks.title: '/init' and '/code-review' headless
checks.observed: "/init" in a temp project created CLAUDE.md headlessly (6 turns, about $0.005). "/code-review low" in a temp git repo ran headlessly through a background task (task_started, then task_notification) and returned a finding ("div now returns a * b…"). "/review" is listed as its alias. Local commands /context (markdown table), /usage (plan windows), /mcp (summary), /output-style and /effort (usage) answer with num_turns 0.
checks.designImpact: Confirms passthrough for init (generates CLAUDE.md) and review ("/code-review <target>"). Note that code-review runs in a background task, so its result arrives via task_notification plus the final result. The review card must accept that, and the reaper/Stop logic applies to it.

checks.title: Control methods present in 0.3.295
checks.observed: typeof Query.getContextUsage, mcpServerStatus, toggleMcpServer, rewindFiles, stopTask, applyFlagSettings, setPermissionMode, backgroundTasks, reinitialize, reloadSkills, setMcpServers, supportedAgents, accountInfo, updateSettings, usage_EXPERIMENTAL… are all functions. getSettings() exists at runtime but is undeclared. Exercised: getContextUsage({detail:"summary"}) gives categories and totals. mcpServerStatus() lists the 10 claude.ai connectors. toggleMcpServer(name,false) gives status "disabled", then re-enabled. rewindFiles(u2,{dryRun:true}) gives {canRewind:true, filesChanged:[f.txt,g.txt]}. rewindFiles(u2) restored f.txt to "one" and removed g.txt (needs enableFileCheckpointing:true and the caller-supplied SDKUserMessage.uuid, which is honored in the transcript). renameSession() sets customTitle. forkSession(sid,{upToMessageId:u1,title}) creates a new session holding exactly 1 message. forkSession and renameSession are top-level functions, not Query methods.
checks.designImpact: Confirms rewind via enableFileCheckpointing+rewindFiles, fork via forkSession(upToMessageId), Status via getContextUsage, and MCP via mcpServerStatus/toggleMcpServer. To rewind, the adapter must stamp its own uuid on each SDKUserMessage, because user messages are not echoed back with uuids in the stream.

checks.title: Other contradictions with the design
checks.observed: (1) active_goal is absent from the local stream (C4). (2) Queued "/goal clear" does not cut a running loop (C4c). (3) The SDKUserMessage uuid is not echoed, so rewind anchors must be Sage-generated (C14). (4) SDK MCP tools are deferred behind ToolSearch by default (C9). (5) getSettings() is undeclared (C6). (6) --no-chrome exists as a CLI flag (strings: "--no-chrome Disable Claude in Chrome integration"), so extraArgs {"no-chrome":null} is viable; not exercised. (7) The result message carries fast_mode_state and fast_mode_disabled_reason, as the design assumes. (8) No "rewind" slash command in the list; rewind is only via the control API. (9) Every persisted test session lands in ~/.claude/projects (expected).
checks.designImpact: Update risks[3] and conflicts[0]: GoalSnapshot comes from synthetic messages plus the transcript goal_status, and the budget stop is interrupt then "/goal clear". Add alwaysLoad for Sage MCP tools. Treat getSettings as version-gated.

costNotes: All turns used the user's Claude Max login through the SDK, mirroring Sage cleanEnv. Model claude-haiku-5-5 everywhere except one C6 turn on claude-sonnet-5-5. Summed total_cost_usd (API-equivalent, billed against the subscription) across 27 sessions is about $0.33. The largest were c7 plan mode ($0.12) and the c6 sonnet ultracode turn ($0.10). Workflow/agent fan-out was prevented by denying tools or telling the model not to work.
surprises: active_goal is never emitted to a local SDK stream (CLI gates it on CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE). Goal state is visible only as synthetic messages and transcript goal_status attachments.
The goal loop runs inside a single turn. A queued "/goal clear" waits until the loop ends, so a Sage budget needs interrupt() first.
perTaskStopAffordance absent (Sage today): interrupt() stops background subagents. Present: they survive. Background shells survive either way.
The ultracode keyword triggers only with origin {kind:"human"}. Effort changes without the ultracode key silently turn ultracode off.
SDK MCP tools are deferred behind ToolSearch by default, the handler gets no sessionId, and canUseTool fires for them in default mode.
A slash command is recognized only as the last content block.
The unknown-command fallback goes to the model with or without origin. The design's ordering concern is not reproduced.
q.getSettings() works but is missing from sdk.d.ts.
Plan mode writes ~/.claude/plans/*.md. The test created ~/.claude/plans/task-create-a-file-fuzzy-rainbow.md and test transcripts under ~/.claude/projects/-private-tmp-…-conformance-claude-work-*.
